question: The salary increased by 20%. If the original salary was Rs. 20000, find the new salary.
explanation: An increase of 20% makes the salary equal to 120% of its original value. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New percent}=100\%+20\%=120\%\] | So multiply the original salary by 120/100. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New salary}=20000\times\frac{120}{100}=24000\] | Therefore the new salary is Rs. 24000. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New salary}=24000\]

question: A salary of Rs. 30000 increased by 15%. Find the increase amount only.

question: After a 10% increase, the salary became Rs. 55000. Find the original salary.
explanation: After a 10% rise, the new salary represents 110% of the original. | \[\Rightarrow 110\%\rightarrowRs. 55000\] | So divide Rs. 55000 by 110 to find the value of 1%. | \[\Rightarrow 1\%=\frac{55000}{110}=500\] | Now multiply the value of 1% by 100 to get the original salary. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%=500\times100=50000\] | Therefore the original salary was Rs. 50000. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Original salary}=50000\]

question: Find the equivalent multiplier for a 25% increase in the salary.
explanation: A 25% increase means the new value becomes 125% of the old value. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New percent}=100\%+25\%=125\%\] | Express that new percentage as a multiplier by dividing by 100. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Multiplier}=\frac{125}{100}=1.25\] | Therefore the equivalent multiplier is 1.25. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Multiplier}=1.25\]
